title: Honest Intervals for Transported Instrumental-Variable Effects with Many Sparse Cells
banked_reason: D0.5.G delivered tier=subfield below novelty_target=field; exact interior normalized logarithmic constant remains open and the constructed upper result is confined to a balanced-cell triangular-array class.
gap_reasons: It does not prove the exact interior normalized logarithmic constant: the Chebyshev achievability coefficient and finite-difference-prior converse coefficient remain unequal, so the delivered result is an order characterization plus an explicit coefficient bracket rather than a sharp-constant frontier.

The projected paper score is constrained by the deliberately narrow balanced-cell triangular-array class, the lack of a transferable upper result for the broader transport model, and the absence of numerical evidence that the alternating growing-order factorial procedure is computationally usable.

[D0.5.G projected paper-score gate: paper_score_ceiling 7.3 < 7.4, so the graded tier 'field' is capped at 'subfield'. The score assesses the delivered research package without credit for unfinished work.]
proof_attempt_summary: Discovery proved finite-sample honest connected intervals for every positive first stage, a same-class two-sided logarithmic minimax order, an interior strength-dependent coefficient bracket, and the nonshrinking weak-first-stage boundary. The D0.5 math and decision panels passed without findings, but the cold novelty reviewer graded the delivered package subfield below the fixed field floor. The exact interior constant and an upper theorem beyond the regular balanced-cell class remain open; no Lean formalization was started.
tldr: This field-level contribution studies a regular-cell submodel of the Chen--Huang transported-IV identification class and proves finite-sample coverage over every positive transported first stage together with upper and lower bounds having the same logarithmic minimax length order.  The audited shared-index variance envelope is \(B_m\le Cn^{-1}\exp\{m\log(m+1)+Cm\}\), including reused target observations.  Chebyshev tuning gives the achievable beta-indexed coefficient \(\kappa_\star(1-2\beta_n)/2\), a legal finite-difference prior supplies the universal upper coefficient \(3\log(3)/2\), and \(H_n(a_n)\asymp1\) when \(\sqrt n\,a_n=O(1)\).  The two interior coefficients are not proved equal.
gap: Regular transported-CACE methods identify the target ratio under an integrated first-stage transport condition but do not justify inference when the number of adjustment cells is proportional to sample size and the transported first stage can vanish.  Randomization-exact LATE methods require a known assignment design and obtain finite-sample exactness under effect homogeneity, while sparse-discrete causal theory does not provide globally honest inference for this transported IV ratio.
fill: The project constructs an observable finite-sample score interval and an explicit interpolation-uniform prior-to-length lemma, then proves a same-class all-connected-interval converse that matches the upper bound on the logarithmic scale uniformly over polynomially weak target compliance.
